The brief

The decision: — and what is the single thing that, if wrong, sinks your plan?

Pull the real data (don't take the framing above as fact — verify it)

python3 _ingest/edgar.py company <TICKER>
python3 _ingest/edgar.py filings <TICKER> --form 10-K   # Item 1A risk factors + MD&A
python3 _ingest/edgar.py facts <TICKER>                 # XBRL: capex, FCF, cash, debt, margins

Anchor every claim to a real figure. Name the comparables you are judging against.

Canon to bring to bear

canon-... · canon-... · canon-...

Three to five, no more. If you find yourself needing a sixth, the case is too broad. Anything you reach for that is not on this list is exactly what the meta-question is hunting for.

Your deliverable

Full — a 1-page board memo to the spec in README.md: BLUF · the crux · three reasons with real figures · the fatal risk + mitigation · the ask.

Crux-only — the crux in two sentences, plus the one figure that proves it, plus the bear case in one line.

Single-figure call — one number pulled from the filings, what it decides, and your call. Three sentences.

Attach a forecast. One falsifiable statement with a probability and a resolution date, e.g. "70% that gross margin is below X% by FY-end." This is what makes calibration measurable.

Size the call. One line: pass / probe / commit, and why that size fits that probability. A 55% forecast behind "bet the company" fails, and so does a 90% forecast behind "small pilot." See bet-sizing-conviction.
